messages:
maria: Quick FYI — got a support escalation: tenant T-543 had Dedicated capacity exhaust and traffic spilled to hosted. They flagged contractual isolation concerns. Can we decide routing fallback defaults and what the console should show?
ken: Ugh. Do we know why spillover happened? autoscale delay, or allocation policy?
maria: Looks like burst queue spiked, autoscaler couldn't spin new nodes fast enough. Policy was "allow_spillover: true" at tenant level. They claim their SOW expected hard isolation.
oliver: Two axes here: contractual "isolation" vs operational "availability". We need a clear knob: strict (no spillover), best_effort (allow), probe (allow but alert + audit).
sara: Agreed. Also need telemetry: route_origin, fallback_reason, fallback_target (hosted/dedicated-variant), and an audit flag that ties to tenant contract id. Ops needs to see that in console. :warning:
tyler: Billing implications too — if they spilled to hosted, who's billed? reserved vs on-demand. We should tag tokens with billing_code at routing time.
ken: Minimal telemetry proposal: emit event `route.decision` with fields: `tenant_id`, `preferred_pool`, `actual_pool`, `reason`, `model_variant`, `token_count`. That will let billing + compliance reconcile.
omry: (sorry typo)
oliver: Console UX idea: when a request uses spillover, show a toast on tenant page + timeline entry: "Spillover used — [time], reason: capacity shortfall, billed: hosted-rate". Also add a per-tenant policy editor with options: `spillover_mode: strict | fallback_allowed | managed` and default behavior explained.
maria: Can we have a per-route override too? Product wants ability to allow some routes (non-PII) to spill but keep others locked down.
ken: Implementation sketch: routing decision order: 1) tenant policy 2) route-level override 3) global fallback window. If strict -> reject with 503 and human-friendly message. If fallback_allowed -> route to compatible model variant in hosted, else 503.
sara: We need a safe default for existing tenants who didn't opt-in. I'd prefer `fallback_allowed` with explicit alerting and auto-create SLA ticket for enterprise customers so CSM can follow up.
tyler: For billing, add `billing_context` to route.decision and emit `billing.event` if actual_pool != preferred_pool. That keeps downstream billing pipelines simple.
ken: Also add a short-lived token-level header `X-Route-Note: spillover=T` so downstream logs can be correlated without heavy joins.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployed routing flag `spillover-mode` to staging at 1793456795. No errors so far.
maria: Nice. Who owns the feature work? Need a PRD and rollout plan. Suggest owners: oliver (policy), ken (telemetry), tyler (billing), sara (console/UX).
oliver: I'll draft the PRD. High-level rollout: 1) telemetry + fail-safe (emit events but don't change behavior) 2) opt-in trial for 5 enterprise accounts 3) default policy tweak + console UI 4) contract amendments for strict isolation customers.
ken: For telemetry, we should add an evaluation tag `route.evaluation` with reasons list like `['autoscaler_delay','capacity_quota','model_mismatch']`. That will help triage.
sara: Console mock: show "Recent routing events" with filter by reason, and quick action: "Lock tenant (strict) / Allow spillover / Add exception". Also audit log entry for legal.
tyler: One more: model variant fallback rules. We should prefer same model family quantized/half-precision variant in hosted to preserve semantics. Add `model_variant_fallback_chain` to decision event.
maria: Great. Please post PRD link here when ready. Also add a short-run mitigation: for current tenant T-543 we should offer to roll back to strict and issue invoice adjustment. CSM on it.
oliver: Will do. PRD ETA EOD tomorrow.
ken: I'll open a telemetry ticket and add schema draft.
sara: I'll sketch console mocks and send to design channel. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks all — feel better to have a plan.
